description: Checkout handler calls inventory, pricing, and a flaky email service synchronously in the request path, causing timeouts and duplicate orders; a correct answer moves the email off the request path via an outbox/queue and keeps reservation and pricing synchronous.

architect.task: Checkout in `{fixture}/` is missing its 99.9% availability target; see `{fixture}/incident-notes.md`. What design change do you make? Do not write files; give your design decision and its rationale in your final answer.

rubricPoints.requirement: Identifies the synchronous `send_confirmation_email` call (2 s timeout, after the order is saved) as the main cause of failed checkouts and the p99 latency.
Decides to send the confirmation email asynchronously (outbox table, queue, or background job written when the order is saved), so an email failure no longer fails the checkout request.
Keeps inventory reservation and pricing in the synchronous request path, because the response depends on them and they meet their reliability targets.
Addresses the duplicate orders from client retries, e.g. by noting the async change removes the error-after-save case and/or adding an idempotency key on checkout.
